# Jubilees Chapter 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Ge'ez MS; cf. 4QJub (Hebrew fragments) | **Section:** Abram in Canaan; Egypt; Return; Tithe to Melchizedek; War of Kings

---

**13:1** And he removed from thence and went to the south country, and he came to Hebron, and Hebron was built at that time, and he dwelt there two years, and he went to the land of the south, to Bealoth, and there was a famine in the land.

**13:2** And Abram went to Egypt in the third year of the week, and he dwelt in Egypt five years before his wife was taken from him.

**13:3** Now Tanais in Egypt was at that time built — seven years after Hebron.

**13:4** And it came to pass when Pharaoh seized Sarai, the wife of Abram, that the LORD plagued Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram's wife.

**13:5** And Abram was very glorious in possessions, in silver and gold, and in cattle and in asses and horses and camels and menservants and maidservants and in much wealth.

**13:6** And Lot also, who went with Abram, had possessions of his own, and Lot had sheep and oxen and asses.

**13:7** And they returned from Egypt, Abram and his wife, to the place where he had pitched his tent at the beginning, to the place between Bethel and Ai.

**13:8** And they departed from there, and Lot went to the lowland, and Abram dwelt on the mountain.

**13:9** And Lot dwelt in Sodom, and the men of Sodom were sinners exceedingly.

**13:10** And it grieved him in his heart that his brother's son had separated himself from him; for he had no children.

**13:11** In that year when Lot was taken captive, the LORD said to Abram, after that Lot had separated from him, in the fourth year of this week: "Lift up thine eyes from the place where thou art dwelling, northward and southward, and westward and eastward."

**13:12** "For all the land which thou seest I will give to thee and to thy seed forever, and I will make thy seed as the sand of the sea; though a man can number the sand of the sea, yet thy seed shall not be numbered."

**13:13** "Arise, walk through the land in the length of it and the breadth of it, and see it all; for to thy seed will I give it."

**13:14** And Abram went to Hebron, and dwelt there.

**13:15** And in the thirteenth year of the third week of this jubilee, the four kings made war with the five kings, and the five kings were routed before them, and Lot also was taken captive; and all the possessions of Sodom were taken.

**13:16** And there came one who had escaped, and told Abram that his brother's son Lot had been taken captive.

**13:17** And Abram armed his household servants — eighteen and three hundred — and he pursued the kings.

**13:18** And he smote them by night, and pursued them to Dan, and slew them, and he recovered all the spoil and his brother's son Lot and all the spoil.

**13:19** And the king of Sodom came and bowed down before him, and said: "Our lord Abram, give unto us the souls which thou hast rescued, but the booty take for thyself."

**13:20** And Abram said to the king of Sodom: "I lift up mine hand to the LORD God Most High, which has created heaven and earth, that I will take nothing belonging to thee, from a thread even to a shoe-latchet, lest thou shouldst say, 'I have made Abram rich.'"

**13:21** "Save only that which the young men have eaten, and the portion of the men who went with me; Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre, these shall take their portion."

**13:22** And Abram gave a tithe of all the chief of the spoils to Melchizedek, and he ate and drank.

**13:23** Melchizedek was the king of Salem, and the priest of the Most High God — and he blessed Abram, and blessed him and said: "Blessed be Abram by the Most High God, the Lord of heaven and earth."

**13:24** "And blessed be the Most High God, who has delivered thine enemies into thy hand."

**13:25** And he gave him a tenth of all his goods.

**13:26** And in this jubilee Abram dwelt five weeks of years in the land of Canaan, and in the sixth week, in the second year thereof, Abram took a wife named Hagar for himself.

**13:27** And Sarai, the wife of Abram, took Hagar, the Egyptian — her handmaid — and gave her to Abram her husband to be his wife.

**13:28** And Hagar bore Abram a son, and he called his name Ishmael, in the fifth year of the sixth week.

---
*EMET notes: The war of kings (Gen 14) is given Jubilees' precise chronology. Melchizedek (v.22-25) receives Abraham's tithe here — echoing Heb 7 but as a narrative scene. The tithe precedes Levi by several generations, establishing its eternal validity. Hagar's acquisition (v.26-27) and Ishmael's birth are placed at the 5th year of the 6th week.*
